Sure, you can achieve this effect by placing your input field and an icon inside a relatively positioned wrapper, and making the icon itself absolutely positioned. Plus, you can assign an event handler to the icon. Here's an example of how you can do it: ```HTML
``` This example displays a text input and a search icon (shown as an SVG here). CSS markup is used to position the icon on the right side of the input field. The handleSearchClick() JS function is called when the icon is clicked, displaying an alert with the current value of the input field. Please note that you need to replace SVG path commands to the icon you want to show up. Also if you use a Framework like React you should consider using 'onClick' or 'onSubmit' events of the form and build a reusable component.
